repository.name: @webex/internal-plugin-calendar
repository.purpose: Internal calendar plugin registered as webex.internal.calendar. It registers the device and Mercury and keeps an in-memory meeting collection current from Mercury calendar create, update, and delete events; lists and syncs meetings for a date window (fetching participants a listing omits); reads notes, participants, and scheduler data; creates, updates, and deletes calendar events with payloads encrypted under a KMS key it creates on first use; and runs free-busy lookups that are sent over HTTPS and answered over Mercury. Its inbound payload transformer decrypts meeting reads through the conversation plugin's decryptTextProp transform.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/internal-plugin-calendar package entry
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package imports the device, encryption, and conversation plugins and registers Calendar as internal plugin 'calendar' with the calendar config and the inbound transformMeetingNotes, transformMeetingParticipants, transformMeetingArray, and transformMeeting payload transformers. The default export is the only export.

public_interfaces.name: webex.internal.calendar runtime methods
public_interfaces.notes: Representative entry points; the full list is the Public surface section of src/docs/README.md. getFreeBusy resolves from a later Mercury event matched by data.requestId and has no timeout. getByType throws for keys other than spaceURI, spaceMeetURL, and conversationId.

public_interfaces.name: calendar plugin events
public_interfaces.notes: Create, update, and delete fire after the meeting collection changes, with the stored or removed item. The JSDoc in src/calendar.js names calendar:meeting:* instead; src/constants.js is authoritative.

public_interfaces.name: calendar configuration
public_interfaces.notes: Defaults are now minus one day and now plus seven days, computed once when the module loads. syncCalendar() without arguments uses them.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not send meeting subjects, notes, webexOptions, attendee fields, or free-busy emails without encrypting them with the plugin's encryptionKeyUrl.
negative_guidance.why: The calendar service stores ciphertext and other clients decrypt with that key.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not send encryptionKeyUrl in a free-busy request that has no emails array.
negative_guidance.why: The encryptFreeBusyRequest JSDoc: the calendar service answers 400 unless the key URL and the sensitive data are both present.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not remove the schedulerData exclusion from the meeting predicates while getSchedulerData decrypts explicitly.
negative_guidance.why: The response would be decrypted twice.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat README.md as the method, event, or error reference.
negative_guidance.why: Its usage block is a placeholder; see docs/adr/0001-retain-product-readme.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not trust the calendar:meeting:* event names in the src/calendar.js JSDoc.
negative_guidance.why: The emitted names are calendar:create, calendar:update, and calendar:delete in src/constants.js.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not run test:unit against a stale dist.
negative_guidance.why: test/unit/spec/calendar.js imports the package by name, which resolves main (dist/index.js).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: The developer confirmed no coverage gate applies; the legacy Jest config sets none.

high.expectation: Source and unit test evidence both support the change, and the behavior has a case in test/unit/spec.

medium.expectation: Only source evidence exists, for example the payload transformer, getFreeBusy, getByType, processMeetingEvent, or attendee encryption. Pin current behavior with a characterization test before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source nor tests settle the question, for example the calendar service's free-busy timing. Stop and report the gap.
